technical_and_design_decisions: Implement Rabbit sink batching as an opt-in configuration with batchingEnabled and batchingSize, preserving the existing one-message-at-a-time behavior by default.
Use the Rabbit client producer batching APIs and ensure pending batches are flushed on normal completion, shutdown, error, and transaction boundaries where applicable.
Provide the Gradle module-build option as reusable build configuration that supports provided Spring XD dependencies, Spring Boot MODULE layout, and the required module packaging conventions.

Extend compression through configurable strategy or codec selection rather than hard-coded conditionals, while retaining the current compression implementation and defaults for backward compatibility.
Make database initialization and database-dependent services conditional so DIRT runtime can start when stream processing does not require database functionality.
Implement the core processor interface contract with an RxJava-compatible adapter and preserve existing processor module contracts and lifecycle semantics.
Add HDFS dataset acceptance tests at the module or runtime integration boundary and include them in the CI test path.
Use existing benchmark scenarios and reporting formats for Rabbit batching and compression so results remain comparable with prior performance snapshots.
Prefer backward-compatible configuration defaults and add focused unit, integration, acceptance, and regression tests for each changed subsystem.
assumptions: The existing Spring XD source repository, build infrastructure, Rabbit sink, HDFS dataset module, DIRT runtime, and relevant test utilities are available and buildable.
The increment targets the existing Spring XD codebase and conventions rather than a migration to a newer Spring Boot or Spring Framework generation.
RabbitMQ and HDFS test environments, or equivalent CI-managed services, are already available; provisioning new infrastructure is excluded.
The requested GitHub issue and pull request references are used as design context, but no external implementation is assumed to be directly reusable without review.
Batching is required only for the Rabbit sink and does not require changes to unrelated Rabbit sources or other sink implementations.
Compression customization requires configuration and extension points, not implementation of new compression algorithms.
The Gradle option is intended to coexist with the existing build and does not require replacing the primary build system.
Baseline benchmark data and scripts exist, and performance work consists primarily of configuring, executing, validating, and recording the requested runs.
Disabling the database requirement applies to DIRT startup and stream-processing scenarios; database-dependent features remain unavailable when disabled.
The RxJava processor contract is a core API addition with compatibility tests, not a complete new RxJava-based processing runtime.
Effort includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, local debugging, CI troubleshooting, and concise documentation, but excludes project management and elapsed waiting time.

activities.activity_description: Inspect the existing build, Rabbit sink, compression configuration, DIRT startup path, processor contracts, HDFS dataset tests, CI configuration, and benchmark harness; identify integration points and define the implementation approach.

Add batchingEnabled and batchingSize configuration, implement accumulation and flush behavior, handle lifecycle and error cases, preserve default non-batched behavior, and add unit and integration coverage.

Add reusable Gradle configuration for module projects, provided Spring XD dependencies, Spring Boot MODULE layout, packaging, repositories, and required boilerplate; validate it with a representative module project.
Create or adapt end-to-end acceptance tests for the hdfs-dataset module, verify data creation and retrieval behavior, integrate the tests with the CI build, and address test isolation and cleanup.

Refactor compression selection behind a configurable extension point, expose override configuration, preserve current defaults and compatibility, and add tests for default and custom compression implementations.
Configure baseline Rabbit benchmarks with batchingEnabled=true and batchingSize=100, execute the scenarios, collect results, compare them with existing snapshots, and record relevant observations.
Configure and execute the baseline Rabbit benchmarks with compression enabled, validate run consistency, compare results with previous snapshots, and record throughput and latency observations.

activities.activity_name: Optional database requirement for DIRT runtime
activities.activity_description: Introduce configuration and conditional startup behavior that allows stream-processing-only DIRT deployments to run without database initialization, while retaining database behavior for features that require it.

Implement the core processor interface contract and RxJava adapter or integration points, define lifecycle and error semantics consistent with existing modules, and add representative processor module tests.

Run the complete relevant test suite, verify interactions among build changes, runtime startup, Rabbit batching, compression, processor contracts, and module packaging, and fix regressions or CI-specific failures.
Document new Rabbit batching and compression options, Gradle module configuration, database-disable behavior, and RxJava processor usage; update examples or reference configuration as appropriate.
Update CI build definitions and test selection, verify repeatable packaging and module installation, inspect generated artifacts, and prepare the increment for review and release integration.
